bib.title: OBELICS: An Open Web-Scale Filtered Dataset of Interleaved Image-Text Documents

question: Can an open, web-scale dataset of filtered interleaved image-text documents be built from Common Crawl and used to train competitive large multimodal models?
hypothesis: Models trained on interleaved web documents outperform models trained on image-text pairs, and an open dataset can match closed ones (implied by the introduction).
contributions: full description of the creation and filtering pipeline
IDEFICS 9B and 80B models trained on it, released with code

method.summary: Pipeline: 25 Common Crawl dumps -> English/dedup/quality text filters -> simplified HTML -> extract interleaved text and images -> node, paragraph and document filters -> dedup and responsible filtering. A Flamingo-style model (frozen LLaMA + frozen OpenCLIP ViT-H, trainable Perceiver resampler and cross-attention) is trained on mixtures to validate it.

datasets.name: OBELICS
datasets.source: Common Crawl Feb 2020-Jan/Feb 2023, CC-BY licence with terms of use
datasets.preprocessing: see summary; thresholds in Table 3 (min 4 words per paragraph, 10 per doc; max 30 images per doc; image side 150 to 20,000 px; aspect ratio within 1/2 to 2; images seen more than 10 times removed)

models.name: IDEFICS-80B
models.architecture: Flamingo-like: LLaMA-65B, OpenCLIP ViT-H-14 630M, Perceiver 126M, cross-attention 13.9B

models.name: 9B ablation models (LAION only, OBELICS only, OBELICS+LAION 50/50)

training.objective: next token prediction plus z-loss 1e-3 x log2(Z)
training.regularisation: gradient clipping 1.0; gradient checkpointing; ZeRO stage 3
training.hardware: 80GB A100: 32 (OBELICS-only, LAION-only) or 64 (mixture) for 9B ablations; 512 for IDEFICS; 128 for IDEFICS-9B; AWS Oregon
training.wall_clock: about 6 days (9B ablations); about 14 days (IDEFICS, IDEFICS-9B)

other.loss_spikes: IDEFICS and 9B LAION+OBELICS each had exactly three restarts from a pre-spike checkpoint with reshuffled data and optionally lower LR
other.qk_norm: layer norm on projected queries and keys in Perceiver and cross-attention

inference.samples: random in-context examples; 0, 4, 8, 16, 32 shots; no seeds or repeats reported
inference.prompting: in-context learning; 0-shot uses 2 priming examples without images; prompts per task chosen from a pool by evaluating 5 intermediate checkpoints (Table 11); rank classification for HatefulMemes and IIIT5k

metrics.name: CIDEr
metrics.definition: captioning on COCO test and Flickr30k test (Karpathy)

metrics.name: VQA accuracy
metrics.definition: VQAv2 testdev, OKVQA val, TextVQA val, VizWiz testdev, open-ended

eval.protocol: no error bars (checklist N/A); single run per config; same eval splits as Flamingo; manual inspection of 250 documents for data quality

prompts.text: {bos_token}Task: Answer the questions based on the image when possible, otherwise say unanswerable.\n
{token_around_image}{image_token}{token_around_image}is an image with written "{context}" on it. Is it hateful? Answer: {class_name}

results.claim: OBELICS holds 141M English multimodal web documents.
results.setup: Common Crawl Feb 2020-Jan/Feb 2023, after all filtering and dedup

results.claim: OBELICS has 353M images, of which 298M are unique (84.3% unique).
results.quote: the final dataset contains 141 million documents and 353 million images, of which 298 million are unique

results.claim: OBELICS has 115B text tokens, versus 43B for mmc4.
Only 60.6% of mmc4 images are unique versus 84.3% for OBELICS.
results.quote: with only 60.6% being unique compared to 84.3% for OBELICS

results.claim: Training 9B models on web documents reaches the same aggregated 4-shot performance with an order of magnitude fewer images than on image-text pairs.
results.setup: 9B Flamingo-style models, LAION only vs OBELICS only vs mix, aggregated 4-shot over 8 benchmarks (read from Fig 6, qualitative)
results.quote: Training on multimodal web documents allows reaching the same performance using an order of magnitude fewer images than training on image-text pairs

results.claim: The LAION-only model degrades on VQA benchmarks during training while the OBELICS model does not.
results.quote: the model trained on image-text pairs slowly degrades through the training

results.claim: The image-text-pair model has a slight edge on captioning, classification and OCR.
results.quote: has a slight advantage performance-wise in captioning, classification, and OCR tasks

results.claim: Mixing OBELICS and LAION beats either alone for a given number of images, tokens or compute.
results.quote: combining the two types of datasets leads to increased performance for a given number of images, tokens, or training compute

results.claim: Manual inspection of 250 documents: 90% have all images clearly related to the text.
results.quote: 90% of the documents have all images clearly related to the text content

results.claim: 30% of inspected documents have images containing written words and 5% structured text.
results.quote: 30% of documents have images containing at least one written word

results.claim: 46% of inspected documents contain faces; 7% have content missed by the filters.
results.quote: 46% of documents contain images with faces

Document filtering funnel: 41.2B docs -> 1.1B -> 365M docs (1.4B images) -> 141M docs (353M images).
results.quote: This process results in 41.2 billion documents

results.claim: Only 55% of 3.6B image links downloaded successfully (about 2B images).
Median OBELICS document has 1 image and 677 tokens; cap is 30 images.
results.quote: a median number of tokens of 677

results.claim: Stricter filters yield fewer documents without higher quality, so users should start from a random subset.
results.quote: using stricter values for the filtering steps yields fewer multimodal documents, although not of higher quality

results.claim: About 3% of docs contain watermarks and 2% logos; no NSFW images found in 250 sampled.
results.quote: Only 3% of documents contain images with watermarks

limits: No error bars or repeated seeds; training runs are single runs.
IDEFICS-9B stays behind Flamingo-9B; at 80B it wins or ties on only 4 of 8 tasks at 32 shots.
The image-text-pair model is better on captioning, classification and OCR; the mixture is best overall.
Filters are heuristic; 7% of sampled documents still had spam or non-English content; PII not intentionally removed; NSFW classifier misflags portraits of women and people of color.
Opt-out cannot be exhaustive; no explicit consent from site authors.
Bias evaluation (FairFace, StableBias) is released with the model, not shown in the paper; men associated more with financial and software terms.
Model comparison confounds data and size: IDEFICS mixture also includes Wikipedia documents, LAION and PMD.
